rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: a reader stuck on an unresolved referent loses the thread. Closest candidate: chunk 1 line 22 'Plus the repo itself (picked next)' — 'the repo' is reused from chunk 0 line 7 ('Come to Module 1 with the repo picked'), in-file carve-out applies; 'picked next' is a reading-order pointer (rule 12 territory, not rule 1) and resolves fine since chunk 2 immediately follows. Chunk 8 line 80 'The bug you picked' resolves to chunk 6's screening step, same file, earlier. No never-named or vague-with-history referents found across all 9 chunks.

Harm check: a reader can't tell which file/section is meant. Two in-body links checked: chunk 2 line 34 '[build one from zero](trainings/.../build-a-project-from-zero.md)' — named by claim, not located by position. Chunk 4 line 49 '[the cohort URL]' — named, not located. Neither points at another file by page position ('the opening lecture said').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: a dead-beat reference strands the reader on something that no longer exists. Prework precedes Module 1, so there are no prior-module beats to reference. Closest candidate, chunk 8 line 80 'The bug you picked' — points at chunk 6 (same file, step 5), which exists and precedes it in reading order. No cross-module 'the X you did/saw' construction present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction (no 'take a guess before...' instruction paired with a narrated outcome) appears anywhere in the body.

Harm check: a slide with only a wait-state/context-dependent bullet projects as saying nothing. Thinnest candidate is chunk 3 (lines 36-42, 'Open a Claude Code session'): even at 2 sentences it carries one self-carrying claim ('Open a new Claude Code session at the repo you just picked. CLI or desktop both work.'). Every other chunk carries substantially more. None are orphans.

Checked all 8 '##' headers against their chunk content: e.g. chunk 4 header 'Get the content folder onto your laptop' (line 43) is followed by exactly that instruction (line 45, fetch the tarball); chunk 6 header 'Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness' (line 58) matches its two-part content (bug screen + readiness check). No header is contradicted by its own chunk.

Checked all five sub-items across all chunks. 'Not X. Not Y. Z.': none found. Anaphora/epistrophe triple: closest candidate chunk 2 line 29 'Real code, real tests, real history' — third leg 'real history' is concrete and distinct (git history, not a repeat of code/tests), stays inside per rule text. Self-grading superlatives: none found (no 'one of the most useful' phrasing). Number + own retraction: none found ('30 to 120 minutes' chunk 1 line 18 is a plain range, not a retraction). Abstraction-noun stacks: none found. Empty-leg verb triplets: none found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE for surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|beat|mood|connections over body (lines 1-83): 2 hits, both 'surface' — chunk 1 line 17 'external or user-facing surface' and chunk 2 line 29 'surface area for rules and memory to land on'. Both are ordinary software/idiomatic usage (a shippable UI/API surface; physical-metaphor 'surface area'), not the repo-internal noun sense ('a writing surface' for a document) rule 8 bans. No compendium/beat/mood/firing/forcing-function hits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 "What to bring": line 20: "**Separate tasks off your backlog.**" — a whole imperative sentence (5 words) bolded, not a noun-phrase handle. The section's four list bullets (lines 15-18, 'Trivial bug', 'A small multi-file task', 'A small feature', 'A bigger piece') read as a menu of task sizes and clear under the reading-list/menu waiver — each bolded lead is a short noun-phrase handle within the ≲5-word cap. This fifth bolded item sits outside that list, is a directive rather than a label, and doesn't match the §34 exception's function (naming a floor+ceiling in one line) or its named headings ('## Prework', '## Bring to Module N', '## Next') — this chunk is headed '## What to bring'. Harm is mild (one extra bold element on an otherwise-clean menu slide) but the rule's own text bans exactly this shape ('never a whole lead sentence').
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Unbold the sentence, or recast as a short handle if it needs to stand out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not mechanically re-verified against the composed deck this run (no headless-Chrome check executed). Structural read: prework.md is a module file under curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/, which the renderer wraps in section.module (per this rule's own architecture note); every '##' chunk sits inside that wrapper, and no phase-less prose section sits outside it in source. This mechanical claim is unverified live; flagging so the maintainer can re-run scripts/slides.test.js or a headless check if this file is suspected of a drop.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` → output: "OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent." Headers '## 1.' through '## 5.' are consecutive; no in-body 'Step N'/'Phase N' cross-references to check.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` → output: "OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut." Confirms the canonical failure this rule cites ('the repo itself (picked in Step 1 below)') is no longer present — current text (chunk 1 line 22) reads 'Plus the repo itself (picked next)', a reading-order pointer, not a page-position one.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule text states explicitly for the open half: 'There is no rule here.' The settled mechanism half is a platform claim, not a per-file editorial check. Both in-body links (chunk 2, chunk 4) are already covered under rule 2 (named, not located).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` → output: "files: 1  slides: 8  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets / oversized: 0 / ✓ every slide is within limits." Slide count (8) matches this judge's chunk map minus chunk 0 (title lede, not scripted as its own slide).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule text scopes the imperative-vs-claim contract to exercise files and lecture files specifically ('Exercise ## headings = imperative or phase label. Lecture headings = claims.'). prework.md's surface-type (per dispatch-preamble derivation: curriculum/trainings/<t>/ → module) is module, not exercise or lecture, so the contract this rule states doesn't bind this file.
